correctness.rationale: For dX=g(X)dB with g=x²/(1+x), f=x/(1+x), a=x²/(1+x)^3, cap C(z)=min(z²,1), Q=exp(fz+(a/2)(C-h)-(f²/2)h), and M_h(x)=E Q(x,sqrt(h)Z)>0. The multiplier Q/M is strictly positive and has conditional mean one. Since |f|≤1 and 0≤a≤4/27, capped exponential tails admit Gaussian moments of every fixed q at every finite h; a Jensen lower bound on M_h(x) uniform in x gives moment induction and genuine martingale, not merely local. At small h the Gaussian tail |z|>1 has exponentially small contribution; Taylor gives a centered Milstein expansion xQ/M=x+gz+(gg'/2)(z²-h)+xρ with Eρ=0, E|ρ|²=O(h³) uniformly. Direct symbolic algebra confirmed x(f²+a)=gg'. Bounded f,a derivatives and Lipschitz g,gg' plus solution moment bounds yield centered Itô–Taylor local error O(h³) in conditional mean-square and global strong order one by discrete Gronwall. The uncapped quadratic Gaussian at x=2 has infinite q-moment for h≥27/(4q); this is a known comparison. Finite quadrature supports but does not certify the stochastic convergence.
